name: Why Can an ADU Cost More Than a Room Addition?

mainEntity.name: What makes an ADU project more expensive than a standard room addition?
mainEntity.text: What makes an ADU project more expensive than a standard room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU often costs more than a standard room addition because it is not just extra square footage; it is a separate living unit with its own functional requirements. That usually means more plumbing, more electrical work, a kitchen, a bathroom, energy-related compliance items, and more detailed permit review. If the unit needs separate access or utility coordination, the cost rises further. A room addition that simply enlarges the main house may be less complex because it does not have to operate independently. Homeowners should compare the long-term benefits of rental income or multigenerational use against the added construction and approval costs. A contractor who understands both project types can help determine which option better fits the property and budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU can cost more because it must function as a separate living unit, which often adds kitchen, bathroom, utility, and code-related requirements. Separate access, plumbing, electrical, energy compliance, and permitting can all increase complexity. A room addition may be simpler if it only expands the main house without creating a full independent unit.
